notes:
TL;DR: Large-scale RAG migration focused on embeddings + learned reranker. Primary concerns: precision@5 regression, indexing cost at 120M documents, and tail latency for user-facing rerank.

Context: Verdant runs an internal search layer over regulatory filings and customer correspondence (~120M doc index, ~4k daily ingestions). Current stack: hybrid dense + lexical; custom in-house embedder (older model) + feature-based reranker. They want to migrate to modern dense embeddings + a learned neural reranker with Redwood to reduce recall noise and improve answer relevance for compliance and sales teams. High sensitivity to even small drops in relevance — quoted: "if P@5 dips by 2% users stop trusting results" (Head of Search).

POC scope and criteria:
- Migrate 50M shard sample to new embedding model + reranker.
- Define evals suite: precision@1/3/5, recall@100, MRR, latency p95/p99 for retrieval+rerank. Redwood Optimize integration required to recommend quantization/batching that preserves quality.
- A/B + canary rollout plan: 5% traffic canary for 2 weeks, automatic rollback if eval metric drops >1.5% or p99 latency > 300ms.
- Cost targets: aim for $0.01-$0.03 per query (including retrieval + rerank). Indexing cost and storage (HNSW shards) need forecast.

- 2025-01-15 discovery call (FF-20250115-0910): validated scale, compliance constraints.
- 2025-01-22 technical deep-dive with infra + search team (see drive architecture diagram).

Open technical notes:

- Reranker model: prefer reranker that supports early exit and token-level cost controls; discuss quantized 4-bit option as cost mitigation but must run evals to measure quality delta.
- Monitoring: require token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and regression alerts tied to eval baselines.

Sales notes: Strong enterprise potential if POC meets quality + cost buckets. Close cadence: technical gate (evals) -> procurement (legal, SOW) -> onboarding (dedicated capacity).
